title: Lexical Onramp Frontdoor: Hybrid Prefix Cache + Heuristic Gating for Prompt Preprocessing
creator: Priya Rao
description:
Problem: Prefill-side preprocessing (prompt normalization, segmentation, and prefix handling) dominates tail latency for short prompts in our hosted API. The current pipeline performs full Unicode normalization, regex-based whitespace normalization, and a monolithic tokenization pass even for common short ASCII prompts. This increases CPU latency, stalls the decode hot path, and defeats attention-kernel choices that expect low prefill overhead.

Proposal: Implement a 'Lexical Onramp Frontdoor'—a small, low-latency fast-path that is evaluated before the full tokenizer. The onramp consists of three components: a compact session-scoped prefix cache (hybrid: tiny in-memory open-addressing hash + compact fingerprint index), an ASCII/short-prompt fast-path normalizer, and a heuristic gating layer that selects execution strategy (fast-path, microbatch prefill, or full tokenization). The gating decision is lightweight (2–3 simple checks) and informs downstream kernel selection and decode scheduling: short sequences_hint will prefer low-latency attention kernels and direct decode; long sequences_hint will prefer high-throughput kernels and batched prefill.

Design details: 
- Fast-path normalizer: vectorized ASCII normalization + nil-op for common punctuation; falls back to heavyweight normalizer for non-ASCII or long inputs.
- Hybrid cache: session-keyed prefix cache with TTL; stores pre-tokenized prefix slices and a small metadata fingerprint (utf8-length, ascii-only bitmask, token-count). Cache size is capped per-session to avoid OOM on long-lived sessions.
- Heuristic gating: sample first 64 bytes to decide path; metrics-driven thresholds (token_count_estimate, ascii_fraction, punctuation_density).
- Kernel selection integration: gating writes a short metadata header that runtime kernel router uses to choose attention kernel (low-latency vs throughput) and memory allocation shape.
- Decode scheduling: for expected decode lengths <= 16, prefer immediate decode path with minimal microbatching; otherwise schedule prefill microbatches with adaptive batch size based on recent latency SLO history.
- Eviction policy: frequency-tiered LRU with small per-session write-buffer to reduce contention; background compaction to reclaim slots.

Trade-offs and constraints: 
- Memory vs latency: cache reduces CPU work but increases per-session memory footprint; we cap per-session memory and use TTL to control retention.
- Correctness: fast-path must be lossless for commonly used prompt shapes; maintain deterministic fallback to full tokenizer to avoid semantic drift.
- Observability: must add fine-grained cache-hit metrics and fast-path fallbacks to evaluate real user workloads.

Benchmarks (internal): 
- Short ASCII prompts (<=32 chars): median prefill latency reduced from 9.8ms -> 2.1ms (4.7x). P95 from 28ms -> 7.2ms.
- End-to-end throughput on small prompt workloads improved ~2.8x in our stage cluster.
- Warmup cache-hit ratio observed ~63% after 30k sessions in synthetic mixed workload.
- CPU utilization for prefill path decreased by ~45% on heavy short-prompt load; overall token cost reduced by ~12% due to faster scheduling into low-cost kernels.

Rollout plan: 
1) Feature branch + unit tests + microbench harness (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8342).
2) Integration tests in staging with stress harness (100k short prompts).
3) Canary: 10% traffic in hosted API with dedicated telemetry dashboard (dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/lexical-onramp).
4) Gradual ramp to 50% contingent on P95 latency, cache hit ratio, and error rate.

Acceptance criteria: 
- Fast-path reduces median prefill latency for short ASCII prompts by >=3x in staging.
- No regressions in decode correctness across diverse languages (run full tokenizer conformance suite).
- Cache eviction does not exceed per-session memory budgets under 99th percentile load.
- Metrics emitted: prefill_latency_{p50,p95}, lexical_onramp_cache_hit, gating_decision_distribution, attention_kernel_choice, per-request memory_delta.

Links & artifacts: design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Lexical+Onramp; benchmark harness: github.com/redwood-inference/perf/lexical-onramp; PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8342

comments: 2025-02-11 Priya Rao: Initial spike — sketched gating thresholds and cache layout. Prototype vectorized ASCII normalizer done in rust-lex crate.
2025-02-18 Diego Martinez: Implemented open-addressing prefix cache with 64-entry per-session ring. Benchmarked on staging: median down ~4.2x for simple prompts.
2025-02-22 Code review (Michael Chen): Requested stronger invariants around fallback determinism and added unit tests for surrogate pairs and mixed-language inputs.

2025-02-27 QA (Avery Kim): Found a race under heavy concurrent session writes; fixed by switching to per-session write buffer and background merge. Added stress test PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/perf/pull/129

2025-03-03 Diego Martinez: Canary started at 5% traffic. Observed unexpected increase in cold-start P95 due to TTL eviction oscillation; tuning TTL from 30s -> 90s improved hit ratio. Moving to 10% canary tomorrow.
2025-03-04 Diego Martinez: Added metrics emission hooks for kernel router. Need product review for rollout messaging (PM: add dashboard cards and runbook).
notes: Follow-up work: explore hardware-accelerated unicode normalization (SIMD kernels) and integrate with Redwood Optimize to suggest cache configurations per customer. Also plan to expose per-route gating overrides in Console for enterprise customers with strict latency SLOs.
